L0@P0:  ANNALS OF MATHEMATICS
L1@P0:  Vol. 55, No. 3, May, 1952
L2@P0:  Printed in U.S.A.
L3@P0:  DETERMINANT THEORY IN FINITE FACTORS*
L4@P0:  BY BENT FUGLEDE AND RICHARD V. KADISONt
L5@P0:  (Received May 17, 1951)
L6@P0:  1. Introduction
L7@P0:  In a series of fundamental memoirs on rings of operators [6, 7, 8, 9], F. J.
L8@P0:  Murray and J. v. Neumann classified factors (i.e., central rings of operators)
L9@P0:  by means of a "relative dimension function." They studied, extensively, those
L10@P0:  factors for which this dimension function has a finite range ("finite factors")
L11@P0:  and showed that these factors (and these factors alone) admit a trace function'
L12@P0:  with the standard algebraic properties.
L13@P0:  In an attempt to establish, what seems to us to be a further important algebraic
L14@P0:  property of the trace, viz., the trace of a generalized nilpotent operator is zero,
L15@P0:  and, more generally, the trace of an operator lies in the convex hull of its spec-
L16@P0:  trum, we were led to the introduction of a determinant theory for finite factors.
L17@P0:  This paper will be concerned, principally, with the development of this theory.
L18@P0:  We might note that it is a simple algebraic matter to prove that the trace
L19@P0:  T(N) of a proper nilpotent N is zero. In fact, if N' = 0 and E is the projection
L20@P0:  on the closure of the range of N, then EN = N so that (NE)'-' = N'-'E = 0.
L21@P0:  Then T(N) = T(EN) = T(NE) = 0, by induction on n. That the normalized
L22@P0:  trace lies in the convex hull of the spectrum of a finite-dimensional matrix follows
L23@P0:  at once by bringing the matrix to super-diagonal form, whereby the normalized
L24@P0:  trace appears as the "center of gravity" of the spectrum. This fact together with
L25@P0:  the theory developed in R.O. IV, Chapter IV, yields the same result for operators
L26@P0:  in an approximately finite factor. Furthermore, it is an immediate consequence
L27@P0:  of the spectral theorem that the trace of a normal operator in an arbitrary finite
L28@P0:  factor lies in the convex hull of its spectrum. None of these easily proved facts
L29@P0:  enabled us to conclude the result for arbitrary non-normal operators in non-
L30@P0:  approximately finite factors. However, the general result was established as a
L31@P0:  byproduct of the determinant theory.
L32@P0:  In ?2 we define the determinant on regular operators in a factor of type II1,,
L33@P0:  and establish the properties of this determinant. The proof that the trace lies
L34@P0:  in the convex hull of the spectrum is given in ?3 as an application of the results
L35@P0:  of ?2. The uniqueness of the determinant is established in ?4 by means of an
L36@P0:  algebraic characterization. The final section, ?5, begins with a discussion of the
L37@P0:  normalization which has taken place in the definition of the determinant. A
L38@P0:  * The results of this paper were outlined in a note by the same authors [4].
L39@P0:  t The second named author is a National Research Fellow.
L40@P0:  1 The term "trace" refers, throughout this paper, to the normalized trace which takes
L41@P0:  the value 1 at the identity operator. For a complete account of the theory of factors, the
L42@P0:  reader is referred to the original papers on this subject [6, 7, 8, 91. In making reference
L43@P0:  to these papers, we shall use the abbreviation R.O., I, II, III, and IV.
L44@P0-1:  520 BENT FUGLEDE AND RICHARD V. KADISON 521
L45@P1:  justification for considering only a positive-valued determinant is given in the
L46@P1:  form of various results on the non-existence of characters on the group of unitary
L47@P1:  operators in a factor. The paper concludes with a study of the possible extensions
L48@P1:  of the determinant of ?2 to singular operators in the factor.
